drivers.lead: Cameron and Nasr both reached three at Petit Le Mans in 2024, sharing the same car when they did it
drivers.note: They arrived at Road Atlanta on 12 October 2024 in the #7 Porsche 963 and left it as joint record holders, because until that afternoon nobody had won the overall title more than twice since the series was unified in 2014. Dane Cameron's three came with three different manufacturers — a Corvette DP in 2016, an Acura in 2019, the Porsche in 2024 — and Felipe Nasr's with two, Cadillac in 2018 and 2021 and then Porsche. Neither has won back-to-back titles, and neither defended in 2025: their own team-mates Matt Campbell and Mathieu Jaminet took it. Five drivers sit on two, Pipo Derani and Ricky Taylor among them, so a fourth would put daylight between the record and the field for the first time. Thirteen seasons is a short history, which is exactly why three is enough to lead it.

teams.lead: Cadillac went outright ahead in 2023, the first season of the GTP rules
teams.note: Chevrolet set the pace of the unified era with three straight from 2014 to 2016, and Cadillac — the same manufacturer group under a different marque — matched that in 2021 and passed it in 2023 for a fourth, then took a fifth in 2026. Two of the five are consecutive, 2017 and 2018, both with the DPi-V.R. Acura has three, from 2019, 2020 and 2022. Porsche won the two seasons in between, 2024 and 2025, and Cadillac's 2026 title ended that run. The record is also younger than it looks: this count begins in 2014, when the American Le Mans Series and Grand-Am merged into one championship, so it measures the WeatherTech era rather than the whole history of North American sports car racing.
